answer: A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, as a result paying the pigment bond on all of them and exposing each to the plume slash. Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 11 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. Because the cipher audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. A farm of 240 pays that 193 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
